summary.title: What Software Craftsmanship is about
summary.one_liner: Software craftsmanship is a commitment to stop writing poor-quality code, to go fast by going well, and to practice the discipline like other professionals do.
keywords: how to write better code as a professional
takeaways: The craftsmanship movement started because developers were tired of writing poor-quality software that embarrasses them and their employers.
Speed comes from doing the work well; the post rejects the idea that quick means dirty or that messes can be cleaned up later.
Practitioners commit to writing tests first, testing everything that can be tested, and writing the best code and designs they can.
Code katas, code retreats and practice sessions are presented as ways to improve craft in service of customers, not as navel-gazing.
The clean code wristband is a personal promise to do good work, not a sign of tribal membership.
summary.summary: This is a manifesto-style blog post by Robert C. Martin ("Uncle Bob") responding to earlier critiques of the software craftsmanship movement. It argues the movement's single motivation is weariness with writing bad software, and lists what craftsmen will and will not do, such as making messes to meet schedules and accepting the lie that quick means dirty. It defends practices like code katas and code retreats as professional practice, comparing them to musicians and lawyers who rehearse. The text is opinion and argument rather than technical instruction.
